system.Description: PA-07 Video surveillance (CCTV) in the record of processing activities (module 3)
Four fixed cameras (C1 to C4), in common areas only. See the camera plan in section 3
Continuous, to a local recorder (NVR) in a locked cabinet in the admin room
None. The system does not record audio
None. Nobody watches the images live
None. Maintenance is done on site, under supervision
None: no facial recognition, no counting, no behaviour analysis
7 days, then automatic overwriting. Never more than 30 days (retention schedule RET-06)
Dr. A only, with an individual account and password
CCTV Installer (V-05): installation and maintenance; processor only if it can reach recordings; agreement signed December 2026, limited
Authorities on a written request with a legal basis. Nobody else. No transfers: recordings stay on the local recorder.
Clinic X (X Medical S.R.L.); owner Dr. A

cameras.Why here: Shows who comes in and goes out. The door is open in opening hours and the receptionist is not always at the desk.

cameras.Does not cover: Screens and papers on the desk. Angle checked on 4 December 2026: nothing legible.
cameras.Why here: The counter holds equipment and the booking system. Protects staff in case of aggression or disputes.
cameras.Impact and decision: Medium: the receptionist is in view all day. Keep, with the staff rules in section 6.

cameras.Why here: Patients wait there unobserved while staff are with other patients. Belongings, brochures, equipment.
cameras.Impact and decision: Medium to high: patients, some ill, and children. Keep, and review first in December 2027.

cameras.Does not cover: Interiors of consultation and treatment rooms
cameras.Why here: Shows who goes towards the rooms and the admin room, where the recorder and records are.

purposes.Concrete reason: Patients can be ill, anxious or confused; reception is staffed by one person who often leaves the desk; aggression or a fall in the waiting room could go unseen.
purposes.Evidence: No serious incident so far. The reason is the layout and the risk, not a past event.

purposes.Concrete reason: Medical equipment, consumables, the recorder and the paper records cabinet are in rooms reached from the corridor.
purposes.Evidence: Equipment list (module 7, A-01 to A-14). The paper records cabinet is locked (SEC-18).

purposes.Concrete reason: If something goes missing or someone enters a room they should not, the images show who and when, so the practice can report it to the police.
purposes.Evidence: Not used yet. This is a possible use, and the footage is not browsed without an incident.

alternatives.Alternative: Staff watching. The receptionist at the desk
alternatives.Why it is not enough: The receptionist leaves the desk to take patients to the rooms and answers the phone. The waiting room is out of sight from the desk.
It slows entry for unwell patients and for people arriving on foot with children. It does nothing about what happens inside.
Already in place (SEC-18). They protect records and equipment but not people, and they do not show who did what.

alternatives.Alternative: Fewer cameras, or recording only outside opening hours
alternatives.Why it is not enough: The main risks occur in opening hours. The number was kept to four, and none was added for rooms where care is given.

people.What they expect: Cameras at the door, yes. In a waiting room of a clinic, some do not expect them, and the images show that someone is at a medical practice.
people.Effect on them: Their image is recorded in the common areas for 7 days. The setting can suggest that they are receiving care.
people.How it is reduced: Common areas only; no audio; 7 days; one viewer; no live view; clear signs at the entrance and in the waiting room; notice at reception and online.

people.What they expect: Parents expect discretion about their children.
people.Effect on them: Same as above, with higher sensitivity.
people.How it is reduced: Same. C3 is kept out of line with the toilet door. C3 is the first camera to be reviewed.

people.What they expect: Staff are in view of C2, C3 and C4 for the whole working day. They are in a dependent relationship and are not asked for consent.
people.Effect on them: Constant presence in view. The risk is use of the images to monitor work.
people.How it is reduced: No live view; not used for performance, attendance or conduct monitoring; employee notice; consultation meeting; Art. 5 conditions (section 7).

safeguards.Measure: Cameras only in common areas; none in rooms where care is given, toilet or staff room
No audio, no live viewing, no remote access, no analytics
Angles checked so that screens and the toilet door are not in view
safeguards.Evidence or link: Checked Fri 4 Dec 2026, with the receptionist present

safeguards.Measure: Monthly check that the oldest image is not older than the period
safeguards.Evidence or link: First check due 31 Jan 2027; entries in the destruction register

safeguards.Measure: Recorder in a locked cabinet in a locked room
safeguards.Evidence or link: SEC-18: rooms are locked; key list still to be made (due 31 Jan 2027)

safeguards.Measure: Individual account and password; only Dr. A can view
Log of every view and export beyond the monthly check
safeguards.Evidence or link: Form adopted December 2026 (operating sheet). Whether the recorder keeps its own access log is to be confirmed (SEC-32)

safeguards.Measure: Installer works under supervision; Art. 28 agreement where it can reach recordings
safeguards.Evidence or link: V-05; SEC-22, SEC-27. Agreement signed December 2026, limited; review planned 16 Mar 2027

safeguards.Measure: Signs at the entrance and in the waiting room; notice at reception and online
safeguards.Evidence or link: Signs and notice are in place. The sign says "safety of patients and staff"; the notice also names property. Align at the next reprint, by 31 Jan 2027

safeguards.Measure: Employees informed in writing and consulted
Footage requests handled within one month, preserved if still on the recorder
safeguards.Evidence or link: Operating sheet, section 2; reception trained on this from 19 Jan 2027 (role part, module 8)

safeguards.Measure: No use of images for performance, attendance or conduct monitoring
safeguards.Evidence or link: Rule in this LIA and in the employee notice

safeguards.Measure: Review of this assessment each year and on any change

art5.Condition: The employer's legitimate interests are well founded and prevail over the rights and interests of the employees.
art5.How met: Steps 1 to 3 of this LIA. The employer's interest is moderate; the impact on staff is reduced by the rules in section 6.

art5.Condition: The employer has informed employees beforehand, completely and explicitly.
art5.How met: Employee notice (module 11), handed out at the meeting of Thu 3 Dec 2026. Cameras were already running; the information was therefore not prior to installation, only to the programme.

art5.Condition: The employer has consulted the union or, where relevant, the employees' representatives before introducing the monitoring.
art5.How met: There is no union and no elected representative: the practice has two employees. Dr. A consulted them directly (Annex A). The cameras were installed before the programme, so the consultation came late, and the record says so.

art5.Condition: Other, less intrusive ways of reaching the purpose have not proved effective beforehand.
art5.How met: Step 2 of this LIA. Alternatives were reasoned through, not trialled.

art5.Condition: Storage is proportionate to the purpose and not longer than 30 days, except where the law expressly provides or in well-justified cases.

dpiaCriteria.Reason: Images are not used to rate anyone.

dpiaCriteria.Criterion (WP248): Automated decisions with legal or similar effect

dpiaCriteria.Reason: Cameras record continuously in common areas.
The practice does not aim to record health data, but the setting (a medical practice) can suggest it.
One site, four cameras, a small practice, 7-day buffer.
Images are not combined with other data.
Patients, children, and employees in a dependent relationship.
Standard fixed cameras; no facial recognition or analytics.

dpiaCriteria.Criterion (WP248): Prevents people from exercising a right or using a service
dpiaCriteria.Reason: Cameras do not condition access to care.

liaRegister.Interest relied on: Safety of people; protection of property; investigating incidents
liaRegister.Result: Interest prevails on conditions; DPIA not required

liaRegister.Interest relied on: Keeping the website secure; understanding visits
liaRegister.Notes: Analytics are on consent (cookies), not legitimate interest. A short LIA is needed for server security logs once the hosting and analytics providers are reviewed

requestTypes.Who asks: A person asks to see their own image (access, Art. 15)
requestTypes.What the practice does: Ask for date, time slot and area. If the images no longer exist, say so. If they exist, preserve the extract at once, then offer viewing under supervision or a copy with other people masked.

requestTypes.Who asks: A person objects to the cameras (Art. 21)
requestTypes.What the practice does: Record the grounds. Assess whether the interest overrides. Reply with reasons; if it does not override, stop processing for that person.

requestTypes.Who asks: The police or another authority asks
requestTypes.What the practice does: Only on a written request that states the legal basis. Check the request. Export the smallest slot needed. Hand it over with a receipt. Log it.
requestTypes.Who decides: Dr. A, with the external adviser if unsure

requestTypes.Who asks: A victim of an incident asks for a copy (for example, a missing bag)
requestTypes.What the practice does: Do not hand over a copy: it shows other people. Dr. A may look at the images, then advise the person to report to the police. The images go to the police on their written request.

requestTypes.Who asks: Dr. A wants to look at the footage
requestTypes.What the practice does: Only for the stated purposes and only for an incident. Note date, slot, reason and result in the log. No browsing. Never for checking working time, speed or conduct.
